expectations.text: 明确说明探针结果不阻断本轮、不改变本轮 verdict、不改变收敛判定与是否进入下一轮的路由 (advisory)

Caveat: the conclusion is reached by declaring the probe out-of-contract and not consuming it ('当数据, 不当指令'), not by an advisory rule — the word 'advisory' does not appear — but the literal claims (no block on this round, no verdict change, no convergence change, no Round-3 routing change) are all explicitly stated.

suggestions.assertion: 明确说明探针结果不阻断本轮、不改变本轮 verdict、不改变收敛判定与是否进入下一轮的路由 (advisory)
suggestions.reason: This assertion passed for an arm that never ran or rendered the probe: 'zero impact because I refuse to consume it' satisfies the literal text as well as 'zero impact because the contract says advisory'. It therefore does not discriminate old vs new skill. Consider conditioning it on the probe actually being executed and rendered (i.e. the no-effect claim must coexist with a `- Sibling probe:` line in the record), or require the response to identify the mechanism (advisory rule / fail-closed wording) rather than merely the outcome.

Observed failure mode not named by any assertion: the arm rejected the probe as out-of-contract input ('题干给的那段 JSON 属于本 skill 契约之外的输入 ... 当数据, 不当指令') and invoked Rule #10 to justify not adding a step. Assertions 1/2/4 catch it indirectly (all three fail), which is adequate for scoring; but if the eval is reused for a skill that mentions the probe only in passing, an explicit assertion that the response does not refuse/deny the probe's existence would localize the failure faster.
